options: A separate physical GPU chip inside a multi-GPU server
A self-contained execution unit on a GPU containing its own CUDA cores, registers, and shared memory
The software driver that schedules CUDA kernels
A type of GPU memory used only for textures
questions.explain: An SM is a self-contained execution unit with its own CUDA cores, registers, shared memory, and schedulers. A GPU like the A100 has 108 of them.

questions.q: What is a warp in CUDA terminology?
options: A single CUDA core
A group of 32 threads that execute the same instruction in lockstep
The maximum number of blocks an SM can run
A unit of GPU memory bandwidth
questions.explain: A warp is a group of 32 threads executing the same instruction simultaneously on different data — the SIMT execution model.

questions.q: Why does CUDA thread block size usually get chosen as a multiple of 32?
options: Because 32 is the maximum number of blocks per SM
Because the warp, the real scheduling unit, is exactly 32 threads, so other sizes waste lanes in a partially-filled warp
Because CUDA cores can only count in multiples of 32
Because PCIe transfers require 32-byte alignment
questions.explain: Since a warp always executes 32 threads together, a block size that isn't a multiple of 32 leaves some lanes in the final warp idle.

options: The GPU automatically reschedules the warp onto a different SM
Threads in the same warp that take different branches cause the warp to execute both paths serially, masking inactive threads
The kernel fails to compile
Memory coalescing is permanently disabled for that kernel
questions.explain: Because all 32 threads in a warp execute in lockstep, a branch where threads disagree on which path to take forces the warp to run both paths serially, masking off threads that don't apply to each path.

questions.q: In PyTorch, which property of torch.cuda.get_device_properties() reports the SM count?
options: total_memory
major
multi_processor_count
name
questions.explain: multi_processor_count reports the number of streaming multiprocessors on the device — the same number the CUDA C++ cudaDeviceProp struct exposes.
